concerns.location: plan.md: Phase 4b / research.md 'External hold-out' / spec FR-010, SC-006
concerns.text: The interaction-variance share is computed as 'Σ|SHAP interaction| / Σ|SHAP total|' and reported against the ≥70% criterion as 'proportion of explained variance attributable to pairwise interactions'. Mean-absolute SHAP ratios are NOT a variance decomposition: |SHAP| magnitudes do not sum to R², and this ratio can exceed 1 or be dominated by scale effects. The construct 'proportion of total R² attributable to interactions' is not measured by this statistic. Use a defensible decomposition (e.g., ablation-based ΔR² share, or hierarchical/ANOVA-style decomposition on the hold-out) or restate SC-006 as the SHAP-magnitude ratio it actually is.

concerns.location: plan.md: Phase 1 (temperature retained as predictor) / spec FR-008
concerns.text: Hydrogen diffusion is Arrhenius: log10(D) is approximately linear in 1/T. Including raw 'temperature' as a predictor means the linear baseline will absorb most variance via a single near-deterministic relation, and the ≥70% interaction-share target (SC-006) is close to unattainable by construction. The plan should include 1/T (or log-scale Arrhenius) features and/or explicitly discuss that temperature range differences across materials confound cross-material comparisons (samples measured at different temperatures are not directly comparable observations of a material property).

With ~200 samples, a pre-CV external hold-out plus 5-fold outer CV leaves ~40 hold-out and ~128 training samples per outer fold. The plan flags post-hoc power for the model comparison but does not address power for the hold-out interaction-variance estimate or the ablation ΔR² estimates, which will have very wide CIs at n≈40. Specify how hold-out size is chosen and that interaction-share and ΔR² will be reported with uncertainty, not just point estimates against the 70% criterion.

FR-005 requires 'refitting the full model pipeline on each resample'; the plan fixes best hyperparameters across the 1,000 refits for feasibility. This is a defensible deviation but will understate CI widths (hyperparameter-selection uncertainty excluded). The plan documents the choice but should also state this limitation in the reported CI interpretation (SC-002).

FR-001 requires ingesting data 'from NIST and Journal of Materials Science sources', but the plan's Phase 0 explicitly states no verified open download exists for those sources and substitutes a real-file gate at data/raw/diffusion_measurements.csv. No plan element can satisfy FR-001's named-source ingestion as written; the spec must be amended (the plan's own Scope Correction Request agrees). Until the spec names an obtainable source, FR-001 is unbacked.

FR-009 mandates an a-priori power analysis 'confirming that a sample size of >= 200 satisfies' power >= 0.80 and CI widths <= 0.1. The plan implements only a post-hoc power analysis and treats the a-priori thresholds as targets to check. The a-priori confirmation required by FR-009 has no backing plan element; the spec needs amendment or the plan needs an explicit a-priori design step (e.g., simulation-based power using the schema, clearly labeled as design-time, not results).

FR-005 requires 'refitting the full model pipeline on each resample'; Phase 5 refits at 'fixed best hyperparameters for feasibility, documented'. This is a reasonable, documented deviation, but it weakens FR-005's literal text — either amend FR-005 to permit fixed hyperparameters or add a plan note justifying why hyperparameter re-search per resample is infeasible within FR-006's 6 h budget, so the deviation is spec-sanctioned rather than silent.

concerns.location: plan.md:Summary / Scope Correction Requested vs spec.md:Assumption 'Dataset Availability' and FR-001
concerns.text: The plan and spec are fundamentally incompatible on data: FR-001 mandates ingesting from NIST/JMS sources and the spec assumes ≥200 open-access samples, but the plan states no verified open dataset exists and the pipeline 'produces no result tables' until the spec is amended. The plan cannot satisfy FR-001, FR-009's ≥200-sample basis, or any SC measurement as written. The plan's own scope-correction request confirms this; the spec amendment must be resolved (or the plan restructured around an authorized data-entry path) before this plan is internally consistent with the spec it implements.

FR-005 requires 1,000 bootstrap iterations 'refitting the full model pipeline on each resample'; the plan/research use 'fixed best hyperparameters for feasibility, documented'. This is a deliberate, documented deviation, but it is a cross-doc disagreement with a MUST-level FR that should be reconciled — either amend FR-005 or justify the deviation against the spec's own Computational Constraints assumption explicitly in the plan's FR mapping.

FR-009 mandates an a-priori power analysis confirming ≥200 samples suffice; the plan implements only a post-hoc power analysis and treats the a-priori thresholds as 'spec targets to be checked, not assumed'. The deviation is flagged but leaves FR-009 unsatisfied as written; the plan should state explicitly that FR-009's a-priori confirmation is blocked by the same data-availability gap and fold it into the scope-correction request.

concerns.location: contracts/dataset.schema.yaml:composition vs data-model.md:MaterialSample and plan.md Phase 1
concerns.text: The dataset schema defines composition as 'array of element symbols' with no fractions/amounts, yet Phase 1 computes mean_electronegativity and atomic_radius_variance, which require per-element weights. Neither the schema, the data model, nor the plan defines where composition fractions come from. Add a composition-fraction field (or document the equal-weight assumption) to the schema and data model.

Quickstart instructs 'pip install -r requirements.txt' and the constitution requires a pinned requirements.txt under code/, but the plan's Project Structure tree lists no requirements.txt (or code/ directory — it uses src/). Align the layout naming and include the pinned dependency file in the structure.

concerns.location: plan.md Phase 4b / research.md 'External hold-out' / model_performance.schema.yaml interaction_variance_share
concerns.text: The 'interaction share' metric Σ|SHAP interaction| / Σ|SHAP total| is not a proportion of explained variance (FR-010/SC-006 ask for proportion of total R²). A ratio of mean-absolute SHAP magnitudes is a different quantity, is not bounded to behave like a variance decomposition, and — critically — TreeExplainer's shap_interaction_values includes the DIAGONAL (main effects) in the interaction matrix; if summed naively the numerator double-counts main effects and the share is inflated by construction. Specify off-diagonal-only summation and either a variance-based decomposition or explicitly rename the metric as a SHAP-magnitude share, not 'proportion of R²'.

Post-hoc 'achieved power' computed from the observed effect size (f² from the realized R² gain) is a monotone function of the observed p-value — it adds no information beyond the significance test and cannot 'validate' anything (standard critique, e.g. Hoenig & Heisey 2001). The plan should report the effect size with its CI and the minimum detectable f² at power 0.80 given n, rather than 'achieved power'.

Hydrogen diffusion in metals is Arrhenius: log10 D is approximately linear in 1/T, and temperature typically dominates variance. Including raw `temperature` (not 1/T) as a predictor means (a) the linear baseline is handicapped against the non-linear models for a physically-known monotone relation, inflating the 'non-linear gain' (SC-001), and (b) the ≥70% interaction-share criterion (SC-006) conflates temperature main-effect variance with descriptor interactions. Add 1/T as a feature (or to the linear baseline) and report interaction share net of temperature, or justify the choice.

The hold-out 'interaction-variance check' is computed with the SAME model whose SHAP values defined the interactions — it is an out-of-sample stability check, not an independent validation of the interaction claim. The plan mostly words this correctly ('reported as a measured outcome'), but should state explicitly that SHAP-derived shares are model-internal descriptive quantities and cannot by themselves confirm that interactions drive real-world variance; ablation ΔR² (Phase 5) is the corroborating evidence.

Add 1/T as a feature (or to the linear baseline) and report interaction share net of temperature, or justify the choice.

The hold-out 'interaction-variance check' is computed with the SAME model whose SHAP values defined the interactions — it is an out-of-sample stability check, not an independent validation of the interaction claim. The plan mostly words this correctly ('reported as a measured outcome'), but should state explicitly that SHAP-derived shares are model-internal descriptive quantities and cannot by themselves confirm that interactions drive real-world variance; ablation ΔR² (Phase 5) is the corroborating evidence.

new_concerns.text: The plan defines the primary SC‑006 metric as ablation ΔR² share but does not specify how the ‘without‑interactions’ R² is obtained. If it is computed by zeroing SHAP interaction contributions in the same fitted model, the metric remains dependent on the model’s internal decomposition and may be circular. The plan should explicitly state that a separate model trained without interaction terms (e.g., using only main‑effect features or a depth‑1 tree) will be fitted on the hold‑out to compute R²_without_interactions, ensuring independence of the validation target from the predictor‑derived interaction definitions.

Both raw `temperature` and its reciprocal `inv_temperature` are supplied to all models, with raw temperature retained only for reference. Including both highly collinear features can inflate apparent interaction effects and confound the interpretation of the interaction‑variance share. Clarify whether raw temperature is used in any model; if not, remove it from the predictor set to avoid redundancy, or provide a justification for its inclusion.
